goals: Explain LDA as a projection that separates classes
why: LDA is a fast, stable classifier and a supervised dimensionality-reduction tool, used in face recognition (Fisherfaces), credit scoring and marketing.
explain: **Linear Discriminant Analysis** finds the direction (camera angle) where the class means are **far apart** relative to the spread **within** each class.
Unlike **PCA**, which ignores labels and keeps the directions of maximum total variance, LDA uses the labels to keep the directions that best **separate** the classes.
As a classifier it models each class as a normal distribution with a **shared covariance**, which gives linear boundaries. QDA allows separate covariances (curved boundaries).
With k classes, LDA can reduce the data to at most **k − 1** dimensions, ideal for 2-D plots of 3-class problems.

example.title: Credit default by debt-to-income ratio (illustrative)
steps: One feature, DTI (%): repaid customers average 30, defaulters 50, both with SD 10. 80% of customers repay. Applicant: DTI 44
Equal priors: cut-off = (30 + 50) / 2 = 40 → 44 is above it → predict default (probability ≈ 0.69)
44 is now below the cut-off → predict repaid (default probability ≈ 0.36)
example.result: Because defaults are rare, LDA demands stronger evidence before calling one. If a missed default is very costly, set a lower threshold on the probability instead.

mistakes: Using it with strongly non-normal or very unequal class covariances (try QDA or logistic regression).

practice.code:
from sklearn.datasets import load_wine
from sklearn.discriminant_analysis import LinearDiscriminantAnalysis
from sklearn.model_selection import cross_val_score
X, y = load_wine(return_X_y=True)
lda = LinearDiscriminantAnalysis(n_components=2)
print(cross_val_score(lda, X, y, cv=5).mean().round(3), lda.fit_transform(X, y).shape)
